claims.text: The equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy and the relevant equiatomic quaternary and ternary subsets are single-phase FCC after identical thermomechanical processing.
The quinary alloy has greater lattice distortion than its quaternary and ternary subsets.
Increased compositional complexity in the quinary alloy produces enhanced lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion affects dislocation core structure.
Lattice distortion alters the thermal-activation properties of dislocation slip.
Greater lattice distortion increases local energy barriers for dislocation movement.
Higher barriers to dislocation movement increase effective slip resistance.
The distortion-induced change in the thermal-activation mechanism results in higher flow stress.
The distortion-induced change in the thermal-activation mechanism results in more pronounced strain-rate sensitivity.
Under identical compression tests, the quinary alloy will have higher flow stress than the quaternary and ternary alloys.
Under identical strain-rate-jump tests, the quinary alloy will have greater strain-rate sensitivity than the quaternary and ternary alloys.
The quinary alloy will exhibit lower activation volumes than the quaternary and ternary alloys.
A lower activation volume is evidence of increased strain-rate sensitivity in these tests.
The predicted relationships apply under comparable thermomechanical histories, single-phase FCC conditions, and similar ambient-temperature compression conditions.
Precipitates, grain-boundary effects, and other heterogeneities have only minimal influence under the proposed conditions.
